steps_raw.instruction: Electrode Internal Solution with Biocytin II
Scope and Applicability: Internal solution used for simultaneous patch clamp electrophysiology experiments to probe circuit connectivity.
Potassium Gluconate (C6H11KO7) (Sigma P1847 or equivalent)
HEPES (C8H18N2O4S) (Sigma H3375 or equivalent)
Ethylene Glycol-bis (2-aminoethylether)-N,N,N’,N’-Tetraacetic Acid ([-CH2OCH2CH2N(CH2CO2H)2]2) (EGTA) (Sigma E3889 or equivalent)
Potassium Chloride (KCl) (Sigma P4504 or equivalent)
Guanosine 5’-triphosphate sodium salt hydrate (C10H16N5O14P3·xNa+) (Sigma G8877 or equivalent)
Phosphocreatine (C4H8N3O5PNa2·x H2O) (Sigma P7936 or equivalent)
Magnesium Adenosine Triphosphate (C10H16N5O13P3·Mg2+) (Sigma A9187 or equivalent)
Potassium Hydroxide (KOH):
1N (BDH Chemicals BDH3212-1 or equivalent)
Biocytin (C16H28N4O4S) (Sigma B4261 or equivalent)
Neurobiotin 488 (Vector Laboratories SP-1125 or equivalent)
Sucrose (Sigma S7903 or equivalent)
1.7 ml microcentrifuge tubes (Genesee 24-282 or equivalent)
50 ml conical tubes (Becton Dickinson 352098 or equivalent)
100 ml graduated cylinder designated for Internal Solution preparation
100 ml glass beaker designated for Internal Solution preparation
3 separate 0.45 µm PVDF hydrophilic syringe filters (SLHV004SL EMD Millipore or equivalent)
10 ml luer-lock syringe (BD 309604 or equivalent)
Disposable plastic spatulas (VWR 80081-188 or equivalent)
Osmometer (Fiske 210, Vapro 5600 or equivalent)
Magnetic stir bar remover
30 ml Electrode Internal Solution with Biocytin, pH 7.3, Osmolarity 280-290 mOsm containing:
130 mM Potassium Gluconate
6.35 mM Sodium Phosphocreatine
13.4 mM Biocytin (0.5%)
Warning: Personal Protective Equipment () should be used at all times while operating this protocol. If you are unsure what you should be using, see your immediate supervisor.
Locate stocks of reagents, as necessary and ensure they are under the expiration date. If using new containers of reagents be sure to mark the date of first use.
Keep all temperature sensitive reagents in freezer until needed. When retrieved from freezer, keep on ice constantly.
Obtain a clean stir bar and place it in the glass beaker designated for Internal Solution preparation.
Set up the beaker on the stir plate.
Obtain and fill an ice bucket with regular ice.
Methodology/Procedures: (record all lot numbers and volumes used in the appropriate reagent prep notebook):
To make 30 ml of Internal Solution:
Using a graduated cylinder, measure 50 ml of MilliQ Water. Add the water to an appropriately labeled clean glass beaker containing a clean stir bar.
Place the glass beaker on a stir plate and begin stirring at a high setting (400RPM or higher).
Using a calibrated balance weight out:
0.0224 g (22.4 mg) Potassium Chloride. Slowly add weighed Potassium Chloride to the glass beaker while stirring.
3.044 g Potassium Gluconate. Slowly add weighed Potassium Gluconate to the glass beaker while stirring.
0.238 g (238 mg) HEPES. Slowly add weighed HEPES to the glass beaker while stirring.
0.011 g (11 mg) EGTA. Slowly add weighed EGTA to the glass beaker while stirring.
EGTA takes a significant amount of time to fully dissolve into solution. Cover beaker with clean parafilm to minimize contaminants.
Once EGTA has fully dissolved into solution, place the beaker into the ice bucket. Make sure that stir bar continues to mix solution by shaping the ice around the beaker.
Retrieve Sodium GTP from freezer and rest on ice.
Using a calibrated balance, weigh out 0.0157 g (15.7 mg) Sodium GTP. Slowly add weighed GTP to the glass beaker while stirring.
Continue stirring at a high speed (400 RPM or higher) until all the chemicals are fully in solution.
Table 1: Reagents required for preparation of Internal Solution II
Remove stir bar using a magnetic stir bar remover.
Bring solution to final volume of 100 ml in a clean, labeled volumetric flask using MilliQ water.
Using a graduated cylinder, measure out 30 ml of solution into a beaker with a stir bar and begin stirring at a high setting (400 RPM or higher).
Place the remaining 70 ml of solution in two labeled 50 ml conical tubes in the freezer for future internal solution or fluorescence aliquots.
Retrieve phosphocreatine, Magnesium ATP, and Biocytin from freezer and place in ice bucket adjacent to beaker with internal solution.
Using a calibrated balance, weigh out:
0.0765 g (76.5 mg) Phosphocreatine. Slowly add weighed Phosphocreatine to the glass beaker while stirring.
0.0609 g (60.9 mg) Magnesium ATP. Slowly add weighed ATP to the glass beaker while stirring.
0.150 g (150 mg) Biocytin. Slowly add weighed Biocytin to the glass beaker while stirring.
Alternatively, 0.002 g (2 mg) of Neurobiotin 488 may be used in place of Biocytin.
Using a calibrated pH meter, measure the pH of the Internal Solution. Adjust the pH to 7.3 by adding KOH (1 N) drop wise.
Remove stir bar using a magnetic stir bar remover.
Measure the osmolarity of a 10 µl sample of the solution using an osmometer. If the osmolarity is not 280-290 mOsm, adjust as needed.
If the osmolarity is too high, add MilliQ water.
If the osmolarity is too low, add sucrose.
Confirm that the correct osmolarity has been reached after addition of sucrose or water.
Draw internal solution into 3 separate 10 ml syringes. Attach 0.45 µm filters.
Aliquot ~0.5 ml into each 1.7ml tube.
Store tubes in a freezer box at -20°C.
Label box with reagent name, date, preparer’s initials, osmolarity, and pH.
Record the date of preparation, lot numbers of all components and osmolarity in the reagent prep notebook.
Dispose of excess reagent directly into municipal sewer system.
Wash the stir bar with MilliQ Water.

Rinse all beakers, graduated cylinders, and other equipment used to prepare Internal Solution with MilliQ Water only (No Detergent). Invert all beakers and graduated cylinders and leave on clean absorbent pad to air dry.
Technical Information:
Internal Solution and 70 ml stock expires after 60 days. Store at -20°C until use.

The osmolarity of the Internal Solution normally should not need to be adjusted if all of the components were added correctly. If the osmolarity does need to be adjusted, add MilliQ Water to lower, or sucrose to raise the value.
